title: Trust at First Click? User Acceptance of Digital Consent Interfaces Among Diabetes Patients
summary:
Health apps and wearable devices collect valuable information that can support people living with diabetes, but this data is rarely available to healthcare professionals.
This study tests the Standard Health Consent (SHC), a new digital consent management system that allows people to decide for themselves which health data they wish to share for care or research.

Participants with diabetes will use the GlucoMind App for four weeks. The app includes short weekly questionnaires on emotional well-being and diabetes-related distress. These data can then be managed through the SHC. The study investigates how understandable, user-friendly, and trustworthy this new digital consent system is and whether participants find data sharing meaningful and useful.
conditions: The study involves adult participants with type 1 or type 2 diabetes receiving care at the Department of Diabetology, University Hospital Carl Gustav Carus Dresden. The focus is not on therapeutic intervention but on assessing the acceptance and understanding of a digital consent management system (Standard Health Consent, SHC) in the context of health data use and sharing. Additionally, the study collects information on emotional well-being and diabetes-related distress using the validated DDS-2 and WHO-5 questionnaires.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients over the age of 18 at the Medical Clinic and Polyclinic III of Dresden University Hospital with type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
- Declaration of consent to participate in the study
- Sufficient knowledge of German
- Access to a smartphone, tablet, or computer
Exclusion criteria:
- Inability to give informed consent
- Acute illness that would prevent safe and meaningful use of the app
- Vulnerable groups (children, individuals who cannot give consent, emergency patients, pregnant women/nursing mothers)
